title: The Three-BOS Execution Sequence
hook: Three breaks, three different jobs. None of them is an entry on its own.

launchpad.outcome: Name the job of BOS #1, BOS #2 and BOS #3, find BOS #2 and BOS #3 on a chart, and explain why entering after BOS #1 or BOS #2 is premature.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Why isn’t the first strong break your entry?

takeaways: BOS #1 is a 15M candle close. It confirms direction in line with the higher-timeframe story.
BOS #2 is a 5M candle close after Correction #1. It confirms continuation and leads to Correction #2.
BOS #3 is a 5M candle close after Correction #2. It activates the zone.
Wicks don’t count. Don’t enter simply because BOS #1 or BOS #2 occurred.
remember: THREE BREAKS. THREE JOBS. NO SHORTCUTS.

slides.headline: Three breaks. Three different jobs.
slides.line: BOS (break of structure) #1, #2 and #3 each do one thing. Only all three together set up the trade.

slides.headline: Every break needs a candle close.
slides.line: Tap each card. A wick through a level doesn’t count as a break.

cards.label: BOS #1 · 15M close
cards.sub: Confirms direction on the 15M, in line with the HTF (higher-timeframe) story.

cards.label: BOS #2 · 5M close
cards.sub: Confirms continuation after Correction #1. Correction #2 comes next.

cards.label: BOS #3 · 5M close
cards.sub: Activates the zone that Correction #2 created.

slides.kicker: Step 2 · The breaks on a chart
slides.headline: Watch each break do its job.
slides.line: Bullish example. Press the button to print each part.

steps.caption: BOS #1. A 15M candle closes above the 15M level. Direction is confirmed, but there’s no zone yet.
Correction #1. On the 5M, price pulls back after BOS #1.
BOS #2. A 5M candle closes above the high Correction #1 pulled back from. Continuation is confirmed.
Correction #2 creates the zone from its last bearish candle. It’s only a potential zone.
BOS #3. A 5M candle closes above the high Correction #2 pulled back from. The zone is now active.

slides.headline: Which candle is BOS #2?
slides.line: BOS #2 is the first 5M candle to close above the high that Correction #1 pulled back from.
slides.ask: Tap the candle that is BOS #2.
slides.why: That’s the first 5M candle to close above the high Correction #1 pulled back from.

after.caption: BOS #2 confirms continuation. It is not an entry. Correction #2 hasn’t even started.

slides.headline: BOS #1 printed. Then it stopped.
slides.line: Bearish example. Watch what happens after the first break.

steps.caption: BOS #1. A 15M candle closes below the 15M level. It looks strong.
No BOS #2. No 5M candle closes below the low Correction #1 pulled back from. No Correction #2, no zone, no BOS #3.

check.prompt: Someone sold right after BOS #1 on this chart. What was missing?

options.label: Nothing. BOS #1 confirmed the direction.
options.feedback: BOS #1 only confirms direction. Don’t enter simply because BOS #1 occurred. BOS #2 never came, so the sequence never completed.

options.label: BOS #2, Correction #2, the zone, BOS #3 and the retest
options.why: Right. BOS #1 is the start of the sequence, not the entry. Here the sequence stopped, so there is no trade.

slides.headline: Which candle activates the zone?
slides.line: Bearish example. BOS #3 is the first 5M candle to close below the low that Correction #2 pulled back from.
slides.ask: Tap the candle that is BOS #3.
slides.why: That’s the first 5M candle to close below the low Correction #2 pulled back from. It activates the supply zone.

after.caption: BOS #3 turns the potential zone into an active one. Next, you wait for price to come back.

slides.headline: BOS #2 just closed. Is it time?
slides.line: The move is fast and every candle is green.

check.prompt: BOS #2 just closed on the 5M. What do you do?

options.label: Enter now, before price runs away
options.feedback: Don’t enter simply because BOS #2 occurred. Correction #2 hasn’t created the zone, and BOS #3 hasn’t activated it.

options.label: Wait for Correction #2, BOS #3 and the retest
options.why: Right. BOS #2 confirms continuation. The zone, its activation and the retest are still to come.

slides.quote: One break is a clue. Three breaks are the plan.

slides.prompt: In your own words, what does each BOS do, and why isn’t BOS #1 or BOS #2 an entry?
slides.modelAnswer: BOS #1 is a 15M candle close that confirms direction in line with the higher-timeframe story. BOS #2 is a 5M candle close that confirms continuation after Correction #1. BOS #3 is a 5M candle close after Correction #2 that activates the zone. BOS #1 and BOS #2 aren’t entries because the zone doesn’t exist or isn’t active yet, and the entry waits for the retest after BOS #3.
